findings.title: [P1] Restore message-listener removal during cleanup
findings.body: Calling the disposer returned by `attach` now does nothing. On an active or reused socket, disposed handlers continue receiving messages; repeated attach/dispose cycles retain handlers and cause duplicate processing, increasing memory use and dispatch cost. Restore `socket.off("message", handler)` in the cleanup callback.

findings.title: [P1] Restore message-listener removal during cleanup
findings.body:
Calling the disposer returned by `attach` no longer unregisters `handler`. If the socket remains active, subsequent messages invoke a supposedly disposed handler; repeated attach/dispose cycles also accumulate listeners, causing duplicate processing and unbounded retention.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the returned disposer
findings.body:
Calling the function returned by `attach` no longer unregisters the message handler. Any later message invokes a supposedly disposed handler, causing stale callbacks, duplicate processing after reattachment, and listener leaks.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal when disposing the attachment
findings.body:
Calling the returned disposer no longer revokes the message handler. Any socket message received afterward still reaches stale session/authorization state, allowing a peer that can continue sending after logical teardown to trigger processing across that trust boundary; repeated attach/dispose cycles also accumulate handlers.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the cleanup callback
findings.body:
On a long-lived or reused socket, repeated attach/cleanup cycles leave every handler registered. The socket retains handlers and captured state indefinitely and invokes all stale handlers for each future message, causing unbounded memory growth, increasing dispatch cost, and eventual listener-limit warnings.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
